Incorporating the Beige Book: District reports indicate overall economic activity expanded since February, with labor markets showing increased labor supply and improved quality of job applicants; some firms remain optimistic about future growth. These observations support the FOMC’s characterization of solid growth and strong job gains. Offsetting this, the latest SLOOS shows tighter bank credit and softer loan demand across C&I, consumer, and CRE, implying headwinds for investment and consumption. Netting the Beige Book’s broad-based expansion and labor-market improvement against the SLOOS tightening and stalled disinflation keeps the outlook “cautiously positive,” but modestly stronger than the SLOOS-only read.
